answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and links equivocation evidence across identities. When k coordinated identities equivocate, the protocol scales penalties as O(k^2), so adding identities increases correlated liability rather than diluting it; detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss across the swarm. This makes the fable of costless aliases melt like a glacier on a sunlit terrace.
